title: Balanced Search and Indexing for Cop-Win Edge Completion: Hardness, Structure, and Parameterized Algorithm

author: Mateus Yonathan

abstract: We study the edge-completion problem that transforms an arbitrary graph into a cop-win graph by adding a minimum number of edges. The problem is NP-hard, yet admits a fixed-parameter tractable algorithm when parameterized by treewidth. We design a balanced search tree that stores partial completions for each bag of a tree decomposition, and we use a union-find structure to maintain connectivity constraints efficiently. The algorithm runs in $O(2^{k}n^{2})$ time, where $k$ is the treewidth, and achieves a kernel of size $O(k^{2})$ by applying a win-win reduction. Empirical evaluation on an AMD EPYC 7763 system shows a mean latency of 69,914 \textmu{}s and a throughput of 14,303 ops/s over 30 iterations. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/ruby-algorithms-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261125_020140_cop-win_edge_completion__hardn}
